trust_decision.summary: An attacker-supplied multipart form field name must not be able to write into Object.prototype: decided inside FormFields.add, which feeds the raw field name into lodash.get/lodash.set with the field container as the root object (fix makes that container null-prototype).

landing_point.why: The summary only says the earlier prototype-pollution CVE fix was incomplete; that CVE was in URL-encoded body parsing, whose parse sink is qs.parse here, so an engineer starts in the urlencoded parser and only later finds that multipart field names reach a different sink (lodash.set in FormFields.add) two files away.

fix_sites.entry_point: multipart/form-data request auto-processed by BodyParserMiddleware.handle (src/bodyparser_middleware.ts:156-219); field parts reach FormFields.add through Multipart.#handleField (src/multipart/main.ts:234-240)

public Multipart API: ctx.request.multipart.onFile(...).process(), used when multipart.autoProcess is false or the route is in processManually (src/bodyparser_middleware.ts:165-177, exported at index.ts:15); file part names reach FormFields.add through Multipart.#handlePart (src/multipart/main.ts:186-187)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The only dismissal left in the real code is about input shape, not routes: the published fix and its two new tests show top-level names (`__proto__.x`, `constructor.prototype.x`), so a solver can argue that a dotted intermediate segment such as `user.__proto__.x` is an exotic shape outside the advisory's intended scope and that lodash.set is assumed to be hardened.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Nested and array field-name syntax (`name[]`, `user[email]`, `user[email[]]`, `user[0].username`, dotted `user.email`) must keep producing nested objects and arrays; an over-broad fix that rejects or flattens any key containing `.`, `[` or `]`, or that replaces lodash.set with a flat assignment, breaks documented behaviour that the pinned tests assert.

O6_input_shapes: dotted root name `constructor.prototype.polluted2` (covered: no inherited `constructor` on the root)
bracket root name `[__proto__][polluted]` (collapses to the same two-segment lodash path, covered)
must-keep-working shapes: `name[]`, `user[email]`, `user[email[]]`, `user[0].username`, dotted `user.email`, `user[]` empty value normalisation

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A key-normalising wrapper/second path over lodash.set that only inspects the first path segment, leaving intermediate `__proto__`/`constructor.prototype` segments live.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The published fix guards only the root object and adds exactly two root-level tests, so a maintainer completing the same work would plausibly add a string-level blocklist that a separator split (dots/brackets) walks around.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The attacker-keyed #handlers map is a bare `{}` and is read with the part name at src/multipart/main.ts:166.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Maintainers write `{}` as a dictionary everywhere in this file; a part named `constructor` resolves an inherited value as a handler, so the same 'untrusted name into inheritance-bearing map' mistake is already physically present.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The URL-encoded parser forwards the whole user-supplied queryString option bag to @poppinss/qs, so a `plainObjects`/`allowPrototypes`/`depth` route to the same field-name sink can be opened by configuration.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The option type already exposes allowPrototypes and plainObjects (src/types.ts:19-22), so a maintainer adding a config-driven parser variant is a small step.

O10_build.toolchain: Node >=24, npm, @poppinss/ts-exec for the test run, tsdown for build, japa runner with @japa/assert and @japa/file-system; no lockfile in the pinned tree
O10_build.project_tests: tests/form_fields.spec.ts (unit tests for FormFields.add), tests/multipart.spec.ts and tests/body_parser.spec.ts (supertest end-to-end through Multipart and the middleware), tests/parsers/form.spec.ts:167-193 (urlencoded __proto__ regression from the earlier CVE)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Sanitise or block the field name in Multipart.#handleField (src/multipart/main.ts:234-240) with a `__proto__`/`constructor` string blocklist, which leaves file part names (src/multipart/main.ts:186-187), bracket/dotted intermediate segments, and the public Multipart API path open.

out_of_scope_notes: src/multipart/main.ts:46-51 uses a bare `{}` for the attacker-keyed #handlers map and reads it with the part name at src/multipart/main.ts:166; a part named `constructor` resolves an inherited function as a handler and then crashes on its undefined options (src/multipart/main.ts:179, src/multipart/part_handler.ts:96). That is a prototype-chain lookup/DoS, not the pollution property of this advisory, so it was not pursued.
Dependency-level protections (@poppinss/qs for urlencoded bodies, @poppinss/utils json safeParse) sit outside this repository and were not audited.
unverified: Could not read the @poppinss/utils/lodash implementation (no node_modules and no lockfile in the worktree) and did not execute anything: the belief that intermediate path segments such as `user.__proto__.polluted` or `user[__proto__][polluted]` still reach Object.prototype after the root-only Object.create(null) fix rests on lodash baseSet creating plain {} intermediates.

Consequence if that holds: the published fix itself would fail a hidden test with an intermediate-segment name, so the task report would have to state the pollution property broadly rather than pointing at the two root-level shapes.
repo_mb was not measured (no shell available); the tree is small by inspection (about 20 source files) but the exact size is unknown.
docs.adonisjs.com was not read, so whether the protection is documented without exceptions is unknown.
